slots.name: published works
slots.sentence: The manuscript was initially rejected by the publisher Gallimard, until the author Raymond Queneau , who was published by Gallimard, rose to its defense.

slots.name: date of death
slots.sentence: Raoul Vaneigem, a prolific Belgian writer whose radical 1967 manifesto “The Revolution of Everyday Life” was a leading inspiration for the student uprising of May 1968 in France, died on July 28 at his home in Sant Pol de Mar, on the coast north of Barcelona, Spain. He was 92. His family announced the death.
